images.filename: Map of Northern England with settlements and traditional counties.png
images.caption: Labelled map of cities and some towns of Northern England, along with their traditional county borders. All settlements with at least a population of 60,000 (built-up areas as defined by the ONS as of the 2021 census) are shown on the map, as well as numerous settlements with populations down to 37,000 each. Also labelled are nearby sizeable towns outside the counties but which may be considered culturally or geographically "Northern" as opposed to the Midlands, including Grimsby and Scunthorpe which officially fall within the Yorkshire and Humber statistical region, thus are technically officially part of the North.
images.alt: Labelled map of cities and some towns of Northern England, along with their traditional county borders. All settlements with at least a population of 60,000 (built-up areas as defined by the ONS as of the 2021 census) are shown on the map, as well as numerous settlements with populations down to 37,000 each. Also labelled are nearby sizeable towns outside the counties but which may be considered culturally or geographically "Northern" as opposed to the Midlands, including Grimsby and Scunthorpe which officially fall within the Yorkshire and Humber statistical region, thus are technically officially part of the North.

images.caption:
A bronze pan dating from the 2nd century AD. It was found in a very well-preserved condition with its enamel inlays intact. It is inscribed with the name Aelius Draco and the names of four forts on Hadrians Wall
MAIS (Bowness-on-Solway)
COGGABATA (Drumburgh)
VXELODVNVM (Stanwix)
CAMMOGLANNA (Castlesteads)


Photo by Dominic Coyne, Young Graduates for Museums and Galleries programme August 2007.
